investigate.conclusion:
Yes. In `inject`, when `sampled` is `None`, the code sets `carrier[_SAMPLED]` to the integer `1`.

Relevant lines:

```python
sampled = baggage.pop(_SAMPLED, None)

if sampled is None:
    carrier[_SAMPLED] = 1
else:
    ...
```

- `sampled = baggage.pop(_SAMPLED, None)` — pulls the sampling value out of baggage, defaulting to `None`.
- `if sampled is None:` — the branch taken when no sampling value was present.
- `carrier[_SAMPLED] = 1` — assigns the integer literal `1` (not `True`, not the string `"1"`) to the `x-b3-sampled` header key.

Note there is a second, separate place where `carrier[_SAMPLED] = 1` is also assigned: the later guard

```python
if sampled is flags is (traceid and spanid) is None:
    warn(...)
    carrier[_SAMPLED] = 1
```

That condition is a chained comparison, so it only fires when `sampled`, `flags`, and `(traceid and spanid)` are all `None` — i.e., when nothing at all is being propagated. In the ordinary case where `sampled is None` but trace/span IDs exist, only the first assignment applies. Either way, the value written is the integer `1`.
